full_query: A 26-year-old man presents to the emergency department with fatigue and dark urine over the past day. He was recently diagnosed with cellulitis of his left leg, for which he was prescribed trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole. He denies having nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. He has no significant medical history and does not currently take any medications. His temperature is 98.6°F (37°C), blood pressure is 115/72 mmHg, pulse is 98/min, and respirations are 14/min. Physical exam reveals conjunctival icterus, bilateral flank tenderness, and erythema of the left leg. Laboratory workup is performed, and the results are shown below: Serum: Hemoglobin: 7.2 g/dL Total bilirubin: 2.1 mg/dL Direct bilirubin: 0.8 mg/dL Lactate dehydrogenase: 470 U/L Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase: 7 U/gHb (normal: 6-20 U/gHb) Which of the following would most likely be seen on a peripheral blood smear in this patient? (A) Acanthocytes (B) Codocytes (C) Degmacytes (D) Schistocytes (E) Spherocytes

sentences: Let's analyze the presented case step-by-step to determine which peripheral blood smear finding is most likely
A 26-year-old man with fatigue and dark urine over the past day
Recent diagnosis of cellulitis treated with trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole
Physical exam reveals conjunctival icterus, bilateral flank tenderness, and erythema of the left leg

Laboratory findings: Hemoglobin: 7.2 g/dL, Total bilirubin: 2.1 mg/dL, Direct bilirubin: 0.8 mg/dL, Lactate dehydrogenase (LDH): 470 U/L, Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD): 7 U/gHb (normal: 6-20 U/gHb)
Conjunctival icterus and dark urine suggest hemolysis
Fatigue and low hemoglobin indicate anemia
Elevated bilirubin (mainly indirect) and LDH levels also support hemolysis
G6PD level is at the lower limit of normal which is crucial to consider
The patient was prescribed trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, which is known to trigger hemolysis in patients with G6PD deficiency
G6PD deficiency is an X-linked recessive disorder that predisposes red blood cells to oxidative damage, leading to hemolytic anemia
The oxidative stress from the medication (trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole) triggers hemolysis in patients with this deficiency
In G6PD deficiency, oxidative damage to red blood cells can lead to the formation of Heinz bodies
These damaged cells are often partially removed by macrophages in the spleen, resulting in "bite cells" or "degmacytes" on a peripheral blood smear
Given the above analysis, the most likely finding on a peripheral blood smear in this patient is degmacytes (bite cells)
